seed_ideas.title: In-silico enumeration of capsid–receptor complexes (AlphaFold-class sampling)
seed_ideas.text: Sampling capsid variant × receptor ectodomain pairs (AAVR PKD domains, LY6A/LY6C1, CA4, ALPL, LRP6, glycans) with AlphaFold-class modelling, docking and refinement to test whether a compact, transferable binding-signature class exists; the one AAV application used AlphaFold-Multimer plus RosettaRemodel and found its predicted PHP.C2–LY6C1 pose depend on the AlphaFold-Multimer version (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10115422).
seed_ideas.root_link: Bears on Q1 (measurability) and on whether a compact transferable binding-signature class exists — framer §6.1.
seed_ideas.compute_open: More parallel compute buys model runs/seeds per (variant × receptor) pair; the largest sampling reported in a cited source is 480 AlphaFold2 predictions per target (32 seeds × 5 models × 3 runs) (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-46715-9); above that it is unknown whether more seeds/MSA subsamples converge on one interface footprint or keep alternating, since the only AAV application found the predicted pose change with the AlphaFold-Multimer version (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10115422).
seed_ideas.sequential: none: each (variant × receptor) pair and each seed is an independent prediction job only about three recycle iterations deep, so the enumeration splits directly into independent pieces across GPUs.
seed_ideas.root_question: Can molecular mapping of AAV capsid-receptor interactions on brain microvascular endothelial cells determine which AAV variants transcytose across the blood-brain barrier versus remain intracellular, and for which capsid-receptor binding signatures?
